0.0.n: Add ございます to make this morning greeting polite.

0.1.n: This is part of ございます, which makes おはよう polite; it has no separate English equivalent here.

0.2.n: This completes ございます, the polite ending of the greeting.

1.0.n: This is the first part of the name Youn-a, split across subtitle tokens.

1.2.n: This completes the name Youn-a; it is not the English article.

1.4.n: This is part of the channel name Youn-a TV.

1.5.n: Links the channel name to the people being addressed: its viewers.

1.6.n: A polite way to address a group, here the channel's viewers.

2.0.n: Japanese nouns do not need a plural ending; here it refers to weekends generally.

2.1.n: Marks weekends as the topic of the sentence.

2.2.n: Describes the speaker's usual weekend routine.

2.3.n: Japanese leaves out my here because the relationship is understood from context.

2.4.n: Marks the child as the person accompanying the speaker.

2.6.n: This is what is described as good in the following condition.

2.7.n: Marks 天気 as the thing that would be good.

2.8.n: The if-form of いい, built from its alternative form よい.

2.9.n: Repeats いつも to emphasize the habit of going out when the weather is nice.

2.10.n: Names the destination rather than describing where an activity happens.

2.11.n: Marks 外 as the destination of 出かける.

2.12.n: The plain form comes before ようにする to describe an action the speaker makes an effort to do.

2.13.n: Together with にしてます, this expresses making a conscious effort to maintain a habit.

2.14.n: Connects よう to してます in the pattern for making an effort to do something.

2.15.n: Short for しています; with 出かけるように, it describes an ongoing effort to go out regularly.

3.0.n: Refers to the morning part of the weekend routine.

3.1.n: Sets morning as the topic, contrasting it with noon later.

3.2.n: Names the place the speaker goes in the morning.

3.3.n: Marks 教会 as the destination of 行って.

3.4.n: The て-form of 行く connects going to church with the next activity.

3.6.n: Can mean lunch in other contexts, but here it indicates a time of day.

3.7.n: Marks お昼 as the time of the walk.

3.8.n: Adds contrast to the time phrase, shifting from morning to noon.

3.9.n: Points to the way the speaker is walking now.

3.10.n: The て-form of やる; こうやって together means in this way.

3.11.n: Short for 散歩しています, a polite form describing the routine and the walk shown now.

4.0.n: ついてくる means to follow along; its て-form plus ください makes a polite request.

0.tip: おはようございます is the polite version of おはよう.

1.tip: の links the channel to its viewers, who are being addressed directly.

2.lit: Weekends, always with my child, if the weather is good, I always make a habit of going outside.
2.tip: A verb plus ようにしてます expresses a conscious effort to keep doing something regularly.

3.lit: In the morning, go to church, and at noon, take walks like this.
3.tip: 行って connects the first activity to the next without ending the sentence.

4.tip: A verb in the て-form plus ください makes a polite request.
